Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for the conversation today. As discussed, I attached Redwood’s proposed addendum to the MSA that would enable a localized deployment (on-prem / VPC) for Acme Medical Devices while preserving the licensing boundary and audit access you asked about. High-level goals:

- Allow a customer-hosted runtime (VPC/on-prem) with a limited license for the specified environments and operator accounts.
- Provide an audit/witness pathway that satisfies Acme’s regulators without transferring perpetual source code or unrestricted runtime images.
- Define a narrow, time-boxed snapshot or witnessing procedure for incident & audit purposes (we included a witness-lite option).

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_Addendum_Localized_v1.docx (draft addendum), Acme_Med_Security_Questionnaire_filled.pdf (answers).

Could you please review and send back redlines or comments by EOD Thursday 5/6? If you prefer, we can set a 30-minute call to walk through the sensitive points: scope of license, operator-level access, snapshot custody, and rollback/termination handling.

Next steps on our side: Lauren — legal, please review for negotiation points; Dylan — product/ops, please flag operational must-haves; Karthik — flag commercial impacts.

Thanks,

Jordan —

Appreciate the draft. We reviewed internally and attached our redline (Redlined_Addendum_from_Acme.docx). Main items we changed/suggested:

1) Snapshot / Escrow-like access: we interpreted the witness-lite language as potentially allowing uncontrolled deposit of artifacts. Our redline seeks a documented escrow mechanism or sealed snapshot with a named custodian (we propose SecureHold) and a narrow trigger set for release.
2) Audit window and forensic access: we added specific retention & access windows (30 days notice for non-emergency audits, 48 hours for incident-driven forensic access).
3) Licensing geography: suggested clarifying whether the license is limited to Acme’s US facilities or also to EMEA subsidiaries — we requested explicit territory carveout.
4) Operator evidence: requested sample operational runbooks, evidence of operator-only access, and a certification that operator accounts do not exfiltrate model weights.

We attached the filled questionnaire and a preliminary SOC2 artifact request list to speed validation. We also propose a short session with SecureHold to validate the sealed snapshot workflow.

Please confirm availability for a 30-minute legal + ops call Wednesday 5/5 at 2pm ET or Thursday 5/6 at 10am ET.

Jordan / team —

Thanks for the flag. I read Acme’s redline and sketched negotiation strategy below. High-level: we should avoid any clause that permits the customer to demand a full deposit of runtime images/source or unlimited forensic access. We can offer a bounded, auditable path.

Proposed negotiation points (talking points & redline direction):

1) Sealed snapshot (compromise path):
   - Accept a sealed snapshot held by an independent custodian (SecureHold) only if the snapshot contents are strictly defined (configuration, deployment manifest, image checksums) and explicitly exclude source/model weights or developer build artifacts.
   - Add a technical appendix that lists the allowed artifact types.

2) Triggers & access controls:
   - Define release triggers: (i) regulator subpoena or (ii) mutually agreed forensic investigation with 72-hour review & logged access. Emergency incident can shorten timelines to 24 hours with logged oversight.
   - Include a role-based access matrix for who from Acme (named persons) can request access — require request through procurement/legal with written justification.

3) Audit notice windows & scope:
   - Counter with 10 business days for planned audits, 48 hours for incident triage (to give us reasonable time to coordinate).

4) Territory language:
   - Agree to US-only deployment in the addendum, with a defined path for EMEA expansion (separate SOW/order-form & data residency commitments).

5) Operator evidence:
   - We can provide operator runbook excerpts, role screenshots, and an operator attestation letter signed by our Head of Ops. We should not provide live credentials, full logs containing customer PII, or model weight files.

Commercial fallback: If Acme insists on unrestricted escrow or release triggers we can offer a time-limited professional services engagement (on-prem witness session) for a one-time fee to satisfy auditors.

Action items:
- Lauren: draft counter-redline (high priority) by EOD 5/5.
- Dylan: prepare a 2-page evidence pack template (runbook excerpt + attestation) by EOD 5/5.
- Karthik: prepare a commercial note with suggested PS fee range and impact to deal economics.

I’ll draft suggested clauses now and circulate a counter.

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop

Short note from commercial:

I agree with Lauren’s approach. Practical negotiation path that usually closes: propose the sealed-custodian option (limited artifact types) as baseline; offer a paid on-site witness or PS forensic engagement as a carveout if regulators require deeper inspection.

Suggested pricing: $35k–$60k one-time dependent on engineer-days & geographic travel. If Acme accepts the sealed-custodian path, we keep standard order-form pricing; if they require repeated sight-lines/witness cycles, we include a Service Addendum with rates and a minimum commitment.

If you want, I can join the call with procurement to finalize. I recommend we hold the call on Thu 5/6 10am ET (per Sara’s availability) and have the counter-redline ready beforehand.
